title: Deep learning predicts mortality in a multicenter severe COVID-19 ICU cohort
summary: A deep learning model was assessed in registry data for 900 patients treated in intensive care at 22 Korean centers during 2020–2021. A reduced seven-variable model had an AUC of 0.8247, compared with 0.8500 for the 66-variable model. This is a retrospective prediction result; the study does not establish clinical utility or temporal external validation.
ai_technology: Deep learning mortality prediction model with feature reduction
organization: Chonnam National University Hospital, Gwangju, Korea

evidence.tested: The model predicted mortality from registry data for 900 ICU patients across 22 centers; the seven-variable and 66-variable models had AUCs of 0.8247 and 0.8500, respectively.
evidence.unknown: The retrospective 2020–2021 analysis does not establish prospective clinical benefit or temporal external validation.
evidence.ai_role: The learned deep tabular model estimated mortality risk and supported feature reduction.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
